utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Good morning. Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We are continuing. Mr. Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Lazarevic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Djurdjevic.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We started your examination yesterday and we are about to continue. I'll try to get through my questions as quickly as possible, the questions I prepared for you. The last thing we talked about yesterday is where you lived up to 1992, and you told us that it was in Rijeka. There are a number of related issues that I would like to clarify now. Tell me, please, you lived in Rijeka. What was your job, your occupation there? Excuse me. Should I repeat the question? What was your job, your occupation in Rijeka, while you lived in Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm receiving questions in English. I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... interpretation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, what was your job, your occupation in Rijeka?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was working with the police, with the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were a professional police officer.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just another thing: Can you tell me about your education and your qualifications.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I completed secondary school, training school for police officers, and what was then called the high school for the interior, for internal affairs, which was in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. We can then go on to conclude that you were trained for a police officer, to become a police officer, and that you were a police officer while living in Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you move to Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards the end of 1991, in early December.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you moved to Bosanski Samac, what did you do there?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was unemployed at the beginning, and then I found out that there was an agency in Obudovac and that they needed people to work as military policemen. It was a JNA unit in Obudovac. I went there, I reported to them, and they accepted me. They took me on. And I worked in that unit as a military policeman. And I was receiving salary from them for the work that I was doing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one thing, because it's not reflected in the transcript. You said that you had a contract.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was contractual. I was receiving my salary. As long as I was working, I was receiving salary. When I stopped working, I was no longer receiving salary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think that clarifies it. Tell me, please, the unit in Obudovac, was this part of the 17th Tactical Group of the JNA or not?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was an artillery unit. They had their own commander. As far as I know, it was not part of the 17th Tactical Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, were you perhaps a member of the 4th Detachment in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to talk about the date 16th and the 17th of April, 1992. Where were you then?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Obudovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your family with you?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, they were, my wife and my children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Obudovac?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stayed there until the 20th [as interpreted] of April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. The transcript says the 20th of April. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 28th of April. It was on the 28th of April that I reported to the Secretariat for National Defence in Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Tell me, how did this come about? Why did you report to the Secretariat for National Defence in Bosanski Samac on the 28th of April?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had been informed by the command that I should report there, so I went and reported.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was it that met you there, at the Secretariat for National Defence?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milos Bogdanovic. He was the one who met me there. And he told me that they knew that I had been a police officer, a trained police officer, and that I should report to the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get any written decision on your appointment?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was some kind of work obligation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. When you came to the police station on the 28th of April, 1992, what were your first impressions of the police station when you first came there?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were armed persons wearing police uniforms there. There were some people wearing camouflage uniforms too. There was security outside the station and in the hall. This wasn't the station -- it wasn't like the station that I used to work at before. There were a lot of police officers there, security surrounding the station and in the hall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you began working there, did you find out who the chief of police was?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I reported to the police commander. The deputy was there too. And I knew who the chief was. Mr. Milos Bogdanovic had told me. The deputy commander and the commander were waiting for me there, Milan Bijekic and Savo Cancarevic. And they gave me an assignment. They gave me the job that I was supposed to do. I was to work as duty officer at the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a very short question in relation to that. When you were there at the police station, we used to refer to those people as specials or people wearing camouflage uniforms. Did you see any of those there?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, they were present too. I saw them too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were told that you would work as the duty officer.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the duty officer in service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did that entail exactly? What was your remit as duty police officer? What were you supposed to do?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would receive reports from all over the town and all events that were within the jurisdiction of the police. I would receive persons who were brought in. I would record their presence there if they were detained at the station. In the morning, when a police unit went into the field, I would have the papers from the chief's office, that were forwarded from the chief's office -- the orders from the chief's office would be forwarded to the duty officer's room and then the outgoing patrol in the morning would get those orders from me, from my room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume, of course, that this job is done around the clock at the police station, 24 hours a day, but certainly you were not yourself sitting there for 24 hours straight. Tell me, how was this organised? Did you have shifts?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we took shifts, eight hours each. Between 7.00 in the morning and 3.00 in the afternoon, and between 3.00 in the afternoon and 11.00 in the evening, and then again between 11.00 in the evening and 7.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've explained to us now how these shifts worked. Can you remember, please, in addition to yourself, who else was there working as duty officer?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there was Dimitrije Djordjevic and Ilija Vukajovic [phoen]. I remember those two people. They were also working as duty officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you took shifts with those two people, eight hours each, as duty officers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we took shifts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, during your shifts as duty officer, were any persons brought in?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me, who brought those persons into the police station?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police officers did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it ever happen that specials brought people in, the police officers wearing camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were a man who forwarded orders. Tell me, please, who issued these orders as to which persons would be brought in and which persons wouldn't?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief, the police chief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that Stevan Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whenever a person was brought in, who was it that decided whether the person would be detained at the police station or released?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief, Stevan Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was in charge of guarding those persons who were being held in detention?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police officers were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As we've already had occasion to see here what the SUP building in Bosanski Samac looks like, we've seen what the rooms looked like, can you tell us more specifically, this duty officer's room, just a brief description, please. Where is it inside the building?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's at the entrance. It's at the entrance to the police station. There was a desk to the right and the staircase --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Lazarevic, we had had video footage on the police. Isn't this -- wasn't this the same place?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I didn't want to -- I just wanted to identify, I believe, that Your Honours already remembered that it was one room by the staircase.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So there is no need for repeating this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I have no intention to waste the time of this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, please, during your duty at the police station, during your shifts of duty, did you notice that any prisoners were mistreated?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they being beaten, verbally abused?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it happen during the day, in the evening?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It usually happened in the evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, who was it that came in the evening and beat and maltreated the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people wearing camouflage uniforms, accompanied by Chief Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a number of other things related to certain persons at the police station. Can you please tell us, who was the chief of -- the head of the crime department?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milos Savic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who else worked at the crime department, aside from him?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I came there, when I started to work, Vlado Sarkanovic, also worked there. After a while he left and went to another job, and then Simo Bozic kept on working with Milos Savic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Zaric a member of the police?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Mr. Zaric come to the police station?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So during your shifts, you only saw him once.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, once only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the only time you saw Mr. Zaric, what sort of uniform was he wearing?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was wearing camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This once that you saw him, to the best of your recollection how long did he stay at the police station?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think for about half an hour. I can't really be sure, but I think for about half an hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excuse me. We need to clarify one thing here. When you say camouflage uniform, do you mean the uniform of the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a camouflage uniform that soldiers wore.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we now move to private session for a very brief period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you just mentioned this measure that can be imposed of reporting to the police station, and you mentioned a protected witness who was supposed to report to the police station. What does that mean? You said that that meant that this person had to report to the police station once in the morning at 8.00 and once in the evening at 8.00 p.m. First of all, tell me, who was it that imposed this measure of reporting at the police station?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This measure of reporting at the police station was imposed by the chief of the police station, Stevan Todorovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell me now - of course, without referring to the name of the protected witness - you said that there was a total of five individuals who had this measure of reporting at the police station imposed on them. Can you tell us who the other four persons were Todorovic had ordered this against?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Hadzialijagic, Lamija; Persic, Delista [phoen]; Izetbegovic, Hasan; Tihic, Pasaga.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So that is these five individuals. And now I'm going to ask you about Esma Fitozovic. Tell me, to the best of your knowledge, was she also supposed to report at the police station? Did you see her come in like these other five individuals?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember this person having had this particular measure imposed against her. There is no reason why I would not mention her if I remembered her.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now I would like to ask you about two other situations. Tell me, do you know Kemal Bobic?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, do you remember that Kemal Bobic was brought to the police station? If you remember this, was there anything characteristic that you noticed in relation to Kemal Bobic?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that he was brought in, because this was an extremely tall man and an extremely big man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Tell me now, do you remember whether he was also asked to hand in his documents, to empty his pockets, to take off his shoelaces, that is to say, the procedure that was applied when people were brought into the police station?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Like any other person that was brought in and kept at the police station, again a certificate would be issued --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we've already heard what the procedure was, so let's not dwell on it too long because our time is limited. Tell me another thing now: Do you remember who was the person who brought in Kemal Bobic?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Spasoje Bogdanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, this Spasoje Bogdanovic, does he have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. His nickname is Sole.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I would just like to ask you about one more person: Kemal Mehinovic. Do you remember who Kemal Mehinovic is?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that person. I don't know that individual.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me now: Have you ever seen Milan Simic at the police station? He was one of the accused persons in this case. He was the former president of the executive board and he is now in a wheelchair.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never saw him at the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Lugar and a certain individual called Tihi and Milan Simic beating an individual called Mirsad Jasarevic, nicknamed Bjelko, at the police station? Did you ever see any such thing?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I assume, then, that you could not have participated in something like that yourself.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No way. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me finally: Did Simo Zaric ever issue any orders to you while you were on duty?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Simo Zaric ever say that you should beat someone, you or anybody else at the police station?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could Simo Zaric issue orders to you at all, to you or other persons at the police station?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, tell me, how long did you work at the police station in Bosanski Samac, until when?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until sometime in August 1992. I have a bad back, so the pain in my back returned and I was compelled to remain immobile. However, the pain would not stop. I moved about very seldom. I hardly ever came to the police station. Then I was given a plaster cast for my chest, abdomen, et cetera, so that I could move about easier. I had to wear this cast for a long time. However, even when it was taken off, the pain would not go away, so I was in hospital in Banja Luka --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Our time is really running out. So you did not work approximately in the period until February 1993; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And then I worked all the way up to the 30th of June, 1997, when I retired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Just two more brief questions: While you worked at the police station at that time, did you wear a moustache?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter could not hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they call you Savo Brko [Realtime transcript read in error "Brcko"]?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The answer before that, did he wear a moustache, the interpreters did not hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just repeat the answer to the question whether you wore a moustache.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, would you bear one second with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, here what I see in the transcript, it says "Brcko." There is one C too much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So what is the correct spelling?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: B-r-k-o.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Then it will be corrected. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just ask you something else. That is a very usual nickname for people who wear a moustache in the area that you come from.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question is the following: People who wear a moustache in that area that you come from, Samac, they usually go by the nickname of Brko; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any other counsel? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence of Miroslav Tadic has no questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I see none. The Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The Defence of Blagoje Simic, any questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: He would have said so. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Weiner:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Djurdjevic. My name is Phillip Weiner. I work with the Office of the Prosecutor, and I'm going to ask you some questions this morning. All right? Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, you worked at the police station for approximately four months; isn't that correct? About four months?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I worked at the police station for about four months in 1992, but after my sick leave I returned to the police station and I worked until the 30th of June, 1997, and that's where I retired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, while you were there, you served as the duty officer. You explained you were one of three or more duty officers. And you were able to see as duty officer what was happening at that station because you'd be there pretty much your whole eight-hour shift inside of that station.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But at night, for example, there was no electric light. Yes, I could see what was happening during my working hours, but at night there was no electricity. There were guards there, and you only saw what you could see under those conditions at that time, working conditions. There was no electricity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But by candlelight and flashlight you were still able to see things, you were able to hear things also?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you knew the prisoners -- yes. And you also were able to see and hear what was going on directly across the street at the TO, at the Territorial Defence building, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could hear what was going on. But see? I was staying at the police station because I was the duty officer, and it was my job, and the TO building also had security, and outside the station there were people who were providing security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that prisoners were being brought in by the police and the Serbian volunteers or the Serbian specials, whatever you'd like to call them; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Naser Sejdic was one of those Bosanski Samac police officers that was bringing people in; isn't that correct too?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the specials from Serbia, they were bringing people in. They were arresting people too, in addition to the Bosanski Samac police, such as Naser Sejdic. They were also arresting people, those specials, or they were participating with the Samac police in arresting people, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The specials would occasionally pick someone up. Yes, there was one of them with the police control, but only sporadically it would happen that they brought persons in without the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was mainly the police of Bosanski Samac that was arresting people and bringing them in to you at the duty station.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when we talk about the specials bringing people in, I don't know if you're aware but Simo Zaric has given a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor and he told the investigators in one of his interviews, on June 3rd, 1998, that "The Samac government and Crisis Staff gave Lugar authority to have a special unit to decide who should be detained and placed in the camps." Isn't that consistent with your testimony, that the specials were bringing prisoners in? They were detaining people and bringing them in to you at the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours -- please, don't answer the question. I have an objection. In his previous testimony, the witness never mentioned this. This is only confusing the witness. They said specials were bringing in persons, but the witness never testified that the Serbian authorities in the Crisis Staff gave Lugar the authority to bring detainees into the police station, and that's what the Prosecutor put to the witness as something that he had previously testified to.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I said Simo Zaric, Your Honour, has made that statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. It was clear that it was the interview of Mr. Simo Zaric, Mr. Krgovic. So you're -- your objection is misconceived, actually, and it's a proper question to put to the witness. He can answer that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, Simo Zaric's statement that "The Crisis Staff and the Samac government gave Lugar," one of the leaders of the specials, "authority to have a special unit and decide who would be detained and placed in the camps," isn't that consistent with your testimony that the specials were also arresting and bringing prisoners to the police station?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we have the number -- page of the number and the number of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's P142. I believe it's pages 37 and 38, bottom of 37.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't that consistent with your testimony, sir? Isn't that -- yes, sir. Isn't that consistent with your testimony that they were bringing people in?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether Lugar had obtained any authority from the Crisis Staff, any authorisation. They were bringing people in, but I don't remember that Lugar personally brought anyone in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you have any reason to doubt the validity of Simo Zaric's statement that the Crisis Staff gave Lugar authority to arrest people and bring them to detention in Samac?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I could say anything about that, because I am simply not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, I'm not asking you if you're familiar with the decision. I'm asking you: Do you have any reason to question the validity or the honesty of Simo Zaric's statement that he made that the Crisis Staff and -- gave Lugar -- I'm sorry, the Crisis Staff gave Lugar authorisation to arrest people? Do you know of any reason why Simo Zaric would lie about that? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no doubts about Mr. Zaric's sincerity, but I simply can't answer your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] No, that's all I'm asking you. If you're aware --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm only asking you if you're aware of any bias which would cause Mr. Zaric to lie when he makes that statement. I'm not asking about the information contained therein. Just, are you aware of any bias which would make him lie when he makes that statement? That's all.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Mr. Zaric perhaps has no reason to lie.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I didn't want to interrupt the examination, but I was just informed from my client that if it is possible - and it's just a matter of fairness for them - just when our colleagues are referring to some portions of Mr. Zaric's interview or something like that, if this could be placed on the ELMO because they would know what we are talking about, what page, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're limited in cross-examination. And generally, if it's one phrase or one sentence, we don't place it on the ELMO. If it's paragraphs, I'm happy to do so. If you would like I could do it but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: There's no harm in doing it. You have the document, the ELMO is there, and it's operational.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And he's answered the question. Do you still want to place --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If you are going to continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: No. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, let's continue on: The people who were being arrested, those were Muslims and Croats that were being brought to you each day?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Serbs too were being brought in, not only Muslims and Croats. Well, in fact, in most cases, yes, those were Muslims and Croats, the people that were being brought in, but it did happen that Serbs too were brought in. They would be kept there and then released, same as Muslims and Croats. They would be brought in and some of them were then released.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, the people who were being held at the SUP were non-Serbs, they were Muslims and Croats; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The people who were being beaten and mistreated were Muslims and Croats; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not getting any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll ask the question again, sir. The people who were being held and beaten and mistreated at the SUP or the police station were Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you're aware, sir, that these people were being arrested and held and beaten based on their ethnicity, being Muslims and Croats; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Those persons, for the most part, were brought in because they were members of some of the military units, military units of the SDA or of the HVO. Although, I do remember one person, Zaimbegovic, and I heard that he was not a member of any of the military units. But according to the information we had, the persons being brought in were mostly members of some military units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, you talked about a clergyman who was brought in that you know - without saying his name - was he a member of any military unit?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We had a blind man or a partially blind man testify here yesterday, an Andrija Petric. Was he a member of any military unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Just a matter of clarification. We heard him yesterday. He was never brought in the police station, just -- just that correction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was arrested and brought to the high school. Was he a member of any military unit, the blind man?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know Mr. Petric. I only met him in The Hague. When I came on the 28th of April, he was not brought in then. I don't remember him being brought in. I probably would have recognised him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, having been in the military, are you aware of any military -- any military units or any armies in the world which utilised blind people and issued them weapons?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, Simo Zaric was a signatory of a military document from the command of the 2nd Posavina Brigade. And on page 2, it's P127. It's page -- he indicates that the isolation of Croats and Muslims was followed without any criteria. He's indicating that there was no criteria supporting any of those arrests. Isn't it true those people were arrested because they were Muslims and Croats? That's the only basis for their arrests?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those people for the most part were members of military units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Simo Zaric -- I'm sorry, that same document that Simo Zaric has called you to testify today states -- it's page 4: "Numerous arrests on trumped-up charges." Trumped-up charges, false charges. Again I ask you: Isn't it true that the only reason those people were arrested was on the basis of their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's a repetitive question. It's the third time that actually the same question was posed, whether it was through Mr. Zaric's interview or through some other documents. He's already explained what his knowledge about people who were arrested, and I don't see where this can take us by posing one and the same question four times.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to ask him that and see if he changes his testimony, and then I'm going to ask him that his boss, Stevan Todorovic, who ordered the arrests has indicated that these were unlawful arrests and detentions of the non-Serb population, and ask based on that if the person who issued those arrest orders has said that will he now change his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Simo Zaric has indicated, the man who has called you to testify, in the document he signed that those people were arrested based on trumped-up charges. These were non-Serbs. So again I'm going to ask you: Isn't it true that they were arrested based on their ethnicity? Weren't a lot of those people arrested solely on the basis of their ethnicity, being Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I came from Rijeka in early December 1991. From the 1st of January, 1992 I was mainly staying in Obudovac. I did spend time in Samac occasionally but not too often. I didn't go out very much. I was not particularly well off. I had just moved recently. Therefore, I couldn't know what the situation was like in the town and its surroundings, because I didn't move about that much. And naturally, whenever there was an order by the chief, there was nothing I could do about that. It would have been the same in any police station in the world. It was an order that had to be carried out. It wasn't our decision to make whether we would bring certain people in or not. Ours was to bring them in and then as far as their release was concerned, their potential release, it would have been the chief's decision to make.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your chief, Stevan Todorovic, has pled guilty to committing various crimes, very serious crimes, and he's admitted to the unlawful arrest and detention and confinement of Bosnian Serbs -- I'm sorry, Bosnian Croats and Muslims and other non-Serb civilians in inhumane conditions. Stevan Todorovic, at page 12 of the judgment, his sentencing judgment says, "Stevan Todorovic," the person who gave you those orders to arrest, "has admitted to participating in the unlawful arrest and detention of non-Serb civilians in the Bosanski Samac region." Since the man who gave you orders has admitted that those were unlawful arrests of the non-Serb population, would you agree, sir, that those people were being arrested on the basis of their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we received orders, we carried them out. If Chief Todorovic admitted to this before this Honourable Court, then we were suffering from a delusion. He was my direct superior. He was our chief. I was carrying out his orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you testified, sir, that you were a professional police officer. Let's talk about Todorovic's orders and what was going on in that police station. What you saw in that police station was unlike any other police station you'd worked in; isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, proceed, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, my question to you is: You worked as a professional police officer for most of your career. What you saw in that police station in the spring and early summer of 1992 was unlike anything you'd ever seen previously in any police station; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, but the circumstances were different too. I had been a police officer in peacetime, and this was something completely different. We tried - we did try- we professional police officers to do our job as professionally as possible under those conditions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when, sir, even in wartime conditions, you're not allowed to beat, to torture, to sexually assault prisoners, or murder them; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was not allowed, and we tried to avoid that as far as we could and to suppress that. Whenever we could help people, assist people in anything, we always did invariably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But, sir, you know at that police station that's what was happening; people were being mistreated, people were being beaten, people were being tortured, there was a murder there, and people were being sexually assaulted. We've had uncontested evidence of that in this trial and Stevan Todorovic has admitted to all of those things, your police chief.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In my shift, when I was on duty, there were two cases of mistreatment. It mainly happened when the chief was there. But there had been many more attempts, but we police officers prevented it from happening. We took people somewhere else so they would not be mistreated at the police station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand that, sir. Let me ask you just a few questions, because we have limited time: While you were on duty, while you were the duty officer, there was a very serious incident, there was a murder within, I don't know how many metres, maybe 20 metres from you a man was murdered. Antesa was beaten to death by Stevan Todorovic and other police officers - isn't that true - while you were on duty, 10 metres away, 20 metres away from you a man was beaten to death? Anto Brandic, nicknamed Antesa, July 29th, 1992, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Antesa.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Antesa.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was on duty that evening. And at about 10.00 in the evening, Stevan Todorovic came into the room with four or five persons I didn't know. There was no electricity. We were using candlelight. He asked me, "What's happening?" And I said, "Everything is normal, everything is just as usual." And they all came out into the hall. They opened the door. There was a candle in the hall, one candle perhaps. Then you could hear people moaning and crying for help. You could hear blows. This went on for a while. It lasted for half an hour, perhaps a little longer. I know that it was near the end of my shift when they left and I was getting ready to leave too and to be relieved, and I heard a man moaning, asking for water. I went into the office and this man named Antesa was sitting on the floor, his head against the chair, and he asked me personally to bring him water. I did give him water. He drank some. He thanked me. In the meantime, the new shift had arrived. I left the police station, and it was only the next day that I learned from my colleagues that Antesa had died. However, they did not provide any details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get a good look at Mr. Antesa or -- when you saw -- when you gave him the water? Was he in a bloody condition?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was night-time, candlelights. I couldn't really see him well. I don't think he had suffered any injuries, but that's only as far as I could tell. He drank the water. He thanked me. Nothing more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you --

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then I left the station.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You couldn't see the cross that they carved into his head with a knife? You couldn't see that?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, would you also agree with me in addition to the beatings, the conditions that the prisoners were being held, overcrowded, no shower facilities, no sinks in the room, no beds, these were poor, inhumane conditions? Once again, your chief, Stevan Todorovic, has admitted that the conditions there were inhumane. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me put it this way: Persons who were in one section of the TO, there were beds over there. At the police station there were no beds. However, they were using water and the toilet. No one ever said they shouldn't. They were using even the toilet at the TO building. The policemen put up a makeshift toilet over there using pipes from an electric heater so that people could wash themselves during the summer heat. The water at the TO building, there was a pump. On one occasion, in the morning, they said the pump was out of order, so we brought water there and we mended the pump. We tried to secure at least some decent conditions for those people who were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... decent. But you know those conditions weren't good, and your chief, Stevan Todorovic, has indicated or has admitted that they were inhumane. Isn't that true? Aren't you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Inhumane, yes. But we tried to do the best we could for those people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, sir, you testified about different people coming and going. You said police officers were arresting people, there were guards, police officers also guarding prisoners, volunteers were arresting people, volunteers were in the building, Todorovic was entering and exiting the building. Isn't that true? Isn't that correct, what I've said so far?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he'd go in and out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the -- as did the specials and police officers. Basically everyone had a job. Police officers were guarding, they were arresting people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, that was exactly your previous question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He just answered about Todorovic. I'm just trying to go through the roles of the different people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: He had said yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And then -- yes, they would go in and out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you also noticed -- or let me ask you this: Were you aware that the JNA through the 4th Detachment also had certain functions, they were out guarding the river banks, patrolling, protecting or defending the town? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I just would like to clarify with -- my learned colleague to clarify this question. Is it a question that is separated, guarding of prisoners in the police and guarding banks of the river and -- embankments of the river? I don't see the relation between those two.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just going through the different roles. You had the police doing one function, arresting, guarding prisoners, the JNA had a function, everybody's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The question is quite clear as to which groups the Prosecution is referring to and what they were doing, and he's asking the witness whether the witness was aware of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And while they were doing that, you're aware the JNA also had a role or the 4th Detachment of the JNA; they were out guarding the town, they were on the river banks, in the trenches guarding against an attack?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who was defending the town before I came to the police station. In the meantime, there was an announcement that the JNA was withdrawing from the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina and that --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the Army of Republika Srpska was being established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But before that, before the JNA withdrew and before the 4th Detachment became part of the 2nd Posavina Brigade of the Army of Republika Srpska, you saw JNA soldiers or 4th Detachment soldiers in the town, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you saw Simo Zaric dressed in his JNA uniform come to the police station.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I saw Simo Zaric. But I simply didn't know about how the army was being reorganised. I don't know how that went.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Simo Zaric has testified -- I'm sorry, has given a statement indicating that he would visit the SUP between April 17th and May 1st at two to three hours a day to interview people. And you saw Simo Zaric one day while you were the duty officer at the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we have the page according to the instructions of the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Page 18. Page 18 in --

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Interview of --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Interview of Simo Zaric. One -- I believe it's 141, P141 -- 140? 141.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Can we have it on the ELMO, just to make sure what -- and then again, just one thing: This witness said that on the 28th of April he came first to SUP, so asking him for previous period is just not fair to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: He could have -- he was the duty officer. He spoke to other officers every day. He's there watching everything. He sees Simo Zaric come in. He has to have some knowledge of what's happening there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And if he doesn't know, he can say so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that Simo Zaric had been -- you saw Simo Zaric come in and interview someone while you were there. Were you aware that he had been there almost on a daily basis from April 17th to May 1st and was interviewing prisoners?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I categorically assert that from the 28th of April until I went to hospital I only saw Mr. Zaric once. I don't remember the actual date. I don't know the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Sir, do you have any reason to disbelieve his statement that he was there for two to three hours a day from the 17th of April to the May 1st, his statement? Do you have any reason to --

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, no reason. No reason not to believe it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what he stated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, having been a career -- having been a career police officer, was that common to have members of the military coming into the police stations to interview prisoners?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever seen that happen before, military officers in any of your police stations coming in, interviewing civilian prisoners?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean before, before the war, or are you actually talking about the war, the war operations?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, if there were cases when crimes were committed, when civilian and military authorities worked together, then there was this kind of cooperation, some people were brought in, there were interviews regarding the crimes that had been committed, the evidence that there was, et cetera. I did have such cases. That the military actually addressed the police in relation to the commission of certain crimes, and also if military personnel were committing crimes, there was cooperation, but this was regulated by law.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's what you had in Samac when Simo Zaric was coming in, interviewing civilian prisoners and other people, if they came in from the military to interview prisoners, civilian military cooperation?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: It's a call -- it's a call for speculation. First of all, this witness never said that he knew what Mr. Zaric was doing there. Mr. Zaric could also come to socialise with his friend or something else. How could he answer that? He saw him once, in 30 minutes, he didn't know where he was going and what he was doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. But he had -- but the Prosecution had put the interview statement of Mr. Zaric, where he indicated that he was spending that much time interviewing prisoners, so it follows from there. And Mr. Weiner, your time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I just have two very quick issues, totally two minutes after this, once we finish this police issue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, sir, the fact that Simo Zaric in JNA uniform on that one occasion you saw him but is coming to the police station to interview the prisoners as part of the JNA, that's consistent with what you had seen, civilian military cooperation on investigations, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned a little while ago what kind of cooperation existed between the military and the police, and that was regulated by law. However, I don't know on which basis Zaric came. Perhaps he went upstairs. Nobody informed me, for example, whether he went to see the chief of police or the chief of the crime investigation service. That is something I cannot say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He's given a statement indicating he went there on behalf of the JNA to interview prisoners. Isn't that consistent with civilian military cooperation? He, as a JNA officer, is going to a civilian police station to interview prisoners.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, and these are prisoners that were arrested by Bosanski Samac police, or the specials. That's the only reason they could have gotten there.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that question. Could you somehow express it more specifically. I don't seem to understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If he's interviewing people, prisoners, at that police station, these had to have been prisoners arrested either by your police or the specials, because there was no one else arresting people according to your testimony.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. However, when he was up there, not a single person, at least when I was duty officer, not a single person went up there. I mean, they were on the ground floor and he went upstairs, and not a single person was asked to go upstairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, one more question, and then we'll get off the subject: Was the JNA out arresting people and bringing them to your police station?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, your time is up. I've extended it for five minutes. It's over now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just want to cover two other very quick issues, which will raise, concerning, Kemal Bobic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, Mr. Weiner, your time is up.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. Your Honour, then may I make an offer of proof for an appellate basis?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Because I want to cover -- put on that I would have questioned him concerning certain areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner, you knew very well that your time was limited to so many minutes and you kept on repeating questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It would only be two minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Last two minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just very quickly, sir: You indicated that you talked about Kemal Bobic's arrest and you indicated a person who arrested him. Do you have any records or any diary relating to who arrested whom while you were at the police station? Have you maintained a diary or do you have any records?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you --

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't keep any sort of diary. I'm a retired person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you weren't present when police officers went to Kemal Bobic's house and you don't know who actually went to his house and arrested him, do you?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was brought in by this Spasoje Bogdanovic, nicknamed Sole. There were many policemen whose names and surnames I didn't know. So somebody was probably with him, but I remember that he personally brought him in, but there were so many policemen there whose names I didn't know. I knew them by sight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know who else accompanied that one officer in the arrest of Kemal Bobic?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were three policemen, but I don't know, except for this Spasoje Bogdanovic, I don't know who the other two men were. I know them by sight, but I don't know their names and surnames. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'd like to thank the Court for giving me the extra few minutes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Questions from the other counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Very briefly. Cross-examined by Mr. Pantelic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Djurdjevic, I am Pantelic, Defence counsel for Blagoje Simic. You tried to explain a short while ago and you were interrupted by the Prosecutor that policemen also had problems when they tried to help or when they tried to keep people who wanted to create incidents away from the police station. Could you please complete your thought. What did you want to say when you started out by saying that policemen had problems too? What kind of problems and who created problems for them?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the way it was: Policemen had problems. People came there, civilians. Then people from Serbia came in some kind of uniform. I don't know on what kind of grounds. But at any rate, they came, people in uniform, people in civilian clothes. They were looking for things. They were interested in something. They were under the influence of alcohol. That was the situation. So in that situation, the policemen really tried to protect these people, not to allow them access, and some policemen were even physically attacked, even things like that happened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So let us draw a conclusion. You and your other colleagues had problems that were caused by people, specials, who came to the police station to maltreat people; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order to have a complete picture, I have to put another question to you: The Prosecutor here quoted the statement of Stevan Todorovic, who confessed what he confessed, and you explained what your knowledge in this relation was. With a view to objectivity, I have to tell you that Stevan Todorovic testified before this court that there were arrests of Croats and Muslims because of armed rebellion, because of illegal arming, and that he personally through his services filed criminal charges against these persons to the military court in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object. Does he have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: -- in the transcript that he's referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It was during the cross-examination of Stevan Todorovic in June last year. So it's just a gist of his testimony. And finally, we have also admitted evidence here, a criminal charge signed by Stevan Todorovic against Kemal Mehinovic. This is the exhibit in this -- in this case. So that's a gist that I would like to put to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, can you give us the transcript page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, if you just allow me additional time during the break, because it was just raised -- that matter was raised during the cross-examination of my learned friend, so I can find the transcript during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because the Prosecution would like to make sure that what you have put into the gist is actually correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Okay. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So you can proceed with other questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Djurdjevic, tell me, did you have any knowledge about criminal charges being filed from the Samac police station at the military court in Bijeljina? Did you have any knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Criminal charges were filed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, what is your personal knowledge about this? Did Dr. Blagoje Simic ever take part in the beating of detainees? Did he maltreat people at the police station? What do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is your personal knowledge regarding the following, whether Blagoje Simic ever ordered the arrest and bringing of people into custody at the police station? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I move to strike that. That's outside the scope of cross-examination. I didn't raise anything about Dr. Blagoje Simic. And if he wants to raise it in cross, I'll ask for re-cross about Dr. Blagoje Simic never going there to help any of those prisoners either as a physician.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, maybe I can be more precise Your Honour, no problem with me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tell me, do you know whether the Crisis Staff as an institution ordered the arrest of people?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know, maybe my learned friend Lazarevic has some questions, but I think it's about time for our break. And in the meantime, I will check the transcripts for this particular page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: We'll take our break and continue our proceedings at 11.00 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honours. I am grateful to the Trial Chamber to allow me to make the overview of the previous transcript during the break, and I have some -- some annotations. First of all, during the cross-examination of Mr. Stevan Todorovic by me. It was on June 20th, 2002. Unfortunately, I have only -- only a working version of the LiveNote transcript. It's page 32, line 19 and 24. My question was to Mr. Todorovic whether he filed criminal reports with all relevant documents to the military prosecutor in Bijeljina, and his answer was yes. Then my learned friend Mr. Lukic on several occasions -- first of all, it was June 17th, 2002, also page -- page 17, it's a reference to the working version of LiveNote transcript, line 2 until 5, asked Mr. Todorovic whether criminal reports were submitted to the relevant authorities in military and then before the military court in Bijeljina. Todorovic said yes. Then Mr. Lukic asked him on June 16th, 2002, page 10, line 23 until 25, and page 11, line 1 until 3, whether the criminal reports filed to the military prosecutor throughout 1992 and 1993. He said yes -- Mr. Todorovic said yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think that is sufficient, if those are the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And finally, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just through my learned friend Mr. Lukic on that day, he introduced a criminal report filed by Mr. Todorovic to military prosecution and the exhibit number is D54/3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in this context, Mr. Djurdjevic, you will recall what I asked you a few minutes ago and you have now heard all these details. You heard what Todorovic said under oath before this Trial Chamber. Do you have any reason to doubt the truthfulness of his words when he said that he sent part of the criminal reports filed to the court in Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The criminal reports were sent on to the military prosecutor's office in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djurdjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have finished with my re-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, could the witness just be asked based on page 9114 if he doubts Mr. Todorovic's answer that the Crisis Staff in fact approved this undertaking which were all the arrests? Can the witness be asked that, if he's aware of that, if the Crisis Staff approved it or that he doubts Mr. Todorovic's answer that the Crisis Staff approved the arrests.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You want to put that to the witness now?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Absolutely, in response to the issue that they just raised, Mr. Todorovic's testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, the Trial Chamber does not accept that you should do that. Mr. Lukic, any questions? Mr. Lazarevic, re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will do it very briefly. Re-examined by Mr. Lazarevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During the re-examination by the Prosecutor, Mr. Djurdjevic, you said that there were Serbs as well who were beaten at the police station. Can you tell us, to the best of your recollection, the names of some of these Serbs who had been beaten up at the police station.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jovo Stevanovic, from Samac; Milan Antic, nicknamed Talijan from Samac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The Prosecutor asked you about Mr. Kemal Bobic, and you answered that in addition to this, Mr. Bogdanovic, nicknamed Sole, there were two other policemen that brought him in. I think you said three persons. I apologise. And these were people you knew by sight. Do you know Naser Sejdic nicknamed Cakar?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he among these policemen who brought Kemal Bobic?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, now I'm going to read something to you. I'm going to read it out to you in English, and it has to do with the answers that you gave to the Prosecutor in relation to the arrest of [redacted] and the fact that he had been detained at the TO and the SUP. [In English] "There was one human guard at the TO --"

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Can we go into private session and delete certain names?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That was part of private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Oh, I apologise. It just slipped my mind. I apologise. Can we just go to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: The first question pertains to Mr. Kemal Bobic. What I'd be interested to know is after, as you've told us this morning, after you took Mr. Babic's shoelaces and so on and he went into the room across the corridor, I believe. Is that so? Across the corridor from the duty station where you were.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was down the corridor, down the corridor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Do you know what happened to him after he entered that room, down the corridor from the duty station?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was on duty, nothing happened to him. He was kept like everyone else, and during my shift nothing happened to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: So when you were on your shift, you did not see him taken to see the chief of police, Mr. Stevan Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that. The moment he was brought there and then that he was immediately brought to Chief Todorovic, I certainly don't remember any such thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Did you ever see at some point in time when you were on your shift Mr. Bobic's face, in particular, looking bruised and bloody?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay. Next question: To your knowledge, did Mr. Simo Zaric ever release detained persons from the police station?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Do the names Mr. Jusufovic and Mr. Fadil Sabanovic mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know these people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: And last question: You said this morning that - and I believe this was page 38, line 4 - that the police really tried to protect the detained persons. I'm just wondering why, therefore, when you were on duty in the duty station that you stayed in the duty station hearing Mr. Todorovic and the other persons beating up the man nicknamed Antesa and did nothing. If the police were trying to protect these persons, as you were saying. I'd just be interested to know why it appears from what you've said that you did nothing, apart from giving him water after the event.

utterances.speaker: SAVO DJURDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was the chief, the police chief. And those people who came -- I was only the duty officer. I was not a commander. I was just a police officer, a low-down police officer. My duty was to be there in the duty station, and there were other policemen in the corridor outside. I was the duty officer, and that's where I was supposed to be. There was nothing else I could do. It was my direct superior who actually came. He came to the station. It was my commander, my superior. I was not in a position to order him to do anything. He was in a position to order me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you for giving evidence. We are now finished. You can leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, would it be an appropriate time to address the Chamber with very brief issue --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is it regarding the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, let's finish -- let's hear the next witness first. I did say yesterday that I will give you time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Who is examining the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pisarevic will do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: This is Mr. Goran Buzakovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Precisely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The witness can be brought in. According to the summary, this witness is discussing isolated incident regarding Esad and Safet Dagovic and the collection of weaponry from their house and from the cellar from the same witnesses, from their house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Precisely. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And his time is limited to 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. So Mr. Pisarevic will stick to the limitation that we have and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Because I notice with other witnesses, the summaries were being exceeded. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can the witness make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please sit down. Yes, Mr. Pisarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PISAREVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Examined by Mr. Pisarevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Buzakovic. We have already discussed the way your testimony would unfold. We've discussed the technical aspects. So please, if you could just adhere to everything that we have agreed on. If you have a problem, please let me know. We shall try to keep it as short as possible. Please for the transcript state your first and last name?

utterances.speaker: GORAN BUZAKOVIC
utterances.text: Goran Buzakovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When were you born?

utterances.speaker: GORAN BUZAKOVIC
utterances.text: On the 8th of April, 1965.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
